audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 3 and 4 read Skill and row 6 read Olaf. The already-applied mirror set the lane to Olaf from Level 1 through First item, with Yasuo only at two-plus items.
audit.why: Olaf's early pattern is a genuine stat check — Berserker Rage gives more attack speed and lifesteal the lower he is, Reckless Swing is 325-range true damage every 7s at rank 5, and Ragnarok is CC-immunity while he keeps attacking. Four rows here disagreed with the mirror and would have been overwritten under prose saying the opposite.
audit.corrected: Proposed four paired flips (phases[N].side + win[N]) as one atomic group with matching ratings, plus rewrites of whys[3], whys[4], whys[5], spikes[2].text, content.mid and content.late so no line claims a stage the chart no longer gives.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] described level 5 in the row labelled Level 6, and whys[5] gave Yasuo the first-item spike the mirror assigns to Olaf.
audit.why: Row 4 is Level 6 and row 5 is First item. The flip point in this matchup is two items, not one — Reckless Swing's true damage ignores everything a first crit item buys you.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rewritten as the Level 6 read, whys[5] and spikes[2].text as the first-item read, content.late moved to 'two items on'.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] told the player that late-game Yasuo 'blocks nothing that matters'. Undertow is a projectile and Wind Wall deletes it. No cooldown appeared anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Undertow is Olaf's only projectile and the axe is his entire sticking pattern — picking it back up resets its 9s cooldown, so walling or sidestepping the throw denies both the slow and the reset. Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and 17s at rank 5, which is the number that decides whether you can wall the next axe. Reckless Swing at 325 range and 11/10/9/8/7s is the true damage no resistance answers, and the page was right about that half.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[3].text, spikes[2].text, report[5].t, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns with the real numbers and the correct split between what the wall stops and what it does not.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is titled 'Anti-heal + kite his R' but its body was an unrelated line about Ragnarok being wasted.
audit.why: Berserker Rage scales lifesteal with missing health, so Olaf heals hardest exactly when you have him low — which is why report[8]'s early Executioner's Calling is correct and needed a reason on the page.
audit.corrected: Replaced dosFull[2].d with the missing-health lifesteal reason.

audit.why: Undertow carries a 'grounding — shuts off enemy dashes' derived flag, but Riot's description says only that it reduces Armor and Move Speed. I wrote nothing claiming the axe grounds your Sweeping Blade, and the page never claimed it. Likewise Ragnarok says 'immune to disables' without naming displacement, so I left the existing knockup claim as it stands rather than strengthening it — same call the mirror made.
